title: Fallback Lab: Hands-on Guide for Customer Engineering (Draft)
summary: A compact, runnable slide-deck + facilitator notes for running a 60–90 minute hands-on fallback lab with a customer engineering team. Purpose: demonstrate Redwood's runtime fallthroughs, safe degradations, and model-variant routing in a live environment so platform engineers and integrators can validate recovery options and tradeoffs quickly.
slides:
Title: Fallback Lab — Hands-on Guide for Customer Engineering
Subtitle: Live drills for graceful degradation and decision points
Owner: Aisha Patel — go-to-market ops

Objective slide: What you'll get out of this session
- Validate fallback behaviors end-to-end
- Observe latency and quality tradeoffs under constrained capacity
- Practice operational runbooks for canary failures and model-variant rollbacks

Agenda slide: 60–90 minute flow
- 10m: Context and threat model
- 30–45m: Guided lab (two scenarios)
- 10–20m: Triage & interpretation of metrics
- 10m: Next steps and runbook alignment

Threat model slide: Realistic production triggers
- Regional node outage (simulated)
- Model variant saturation (q-attention fallback)
- Upstream cache invalidation and prefix miss storm

Laboratory setup slide: Environment and access
- Sandbox cluster: ds-fallback-sandbox (pre-provisioned)
- Credentials: ephemeral token in Confluence doc (rotate after session)
- Observability: Console route 'lab-fallback' + local tracing enabled

Scenario A slide: Latency-first fallback
- Trigger: Increase request QPS to force batching pressure
- Expected behavior: runtime routes to smaller context model variant then streams partial responses and kicks a cheaper quantized fallback if latency threshold > 250ms
- Validation checklist: observe per-token latency, fallback log events, streaming flags

Scenario B slide: Quality-preserving fallback
- Trigger: Simulate model quality regression (instrumented)
- Expected behavior: rollback policy routes a subset of traffic to a larger model and routes non-critical routes to cached results; alert raised to on-call
- Validation checklist: side-by-side quality diffs, traced decision path

Lab commands slide: Quick command list (CLI + Console)
- inject-failure --zone=us-west-2 --type=node-terminate
- runtime-route-check --route=lab-fallback --expected=quantized-v2
- curl examples for test payloads (embed sample prompts)

Observability slide: Key signals to watch
- token-latency distribution by model variant
- fallback.invocations metric and last_error
- trace id mapping: request -> decision policy -> final model

Facilitator notes slide: How to run this with a customer
- Start by asking about their SLO priorities (p95 latency vs median)
- Encourage product engineers to call out untested edge-cases
- Use the first 10 minutes to calibrate expectations and scope

Triage & interpretation slide: Common outcomes and actions
- Too many fallbacks invoked: raise batching limits or increase burst capacity
- Quality drop on fallback: enable auto-rollforward to alternate variant or escalate to model-owner
- Observability gaps: add trace hooks and per-route cost tagging

Runbook alignment slide: Post-lab checklist
- Document required routing policies and escalation paths
- Add one canary check to CI that simulates the failure mode used in lab
- Recommend pricing/throughput adjustments for Dedicated customers

Next steps slide: For the customer engineering team
- 1: Share lab report and logs within 48 hours
- 2: Schedule a 30m follow-up to sync on policy changes
- 3: Optional: request a Dedicated capacity pilot for steady-state throughput validation

Appendix slide: Example prompts, curl payloads, and expected logs
- sample_prompt_1: 'Summarize the following text in 2 sentences'
- curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{
  "model": "gptx-lite-quant",
  "prompt": "<sample_prompt_1>",
  "timeout": 7000
}'
